text.p: British retailer Storehouse Plc on Thursday reported a 13 percent increase in underlying first half profits and said it was working hard to reverse a sales decline at its Mothercare childrenswear chain.
Pretax profits before exceptional items rose to 37.5 million pounds ($63.02 million) from 33.3 million. Sales increased 14 percent to 590.5 million pounds from 518.8 million.
The group took an exceptional charge of 20.5 million pounds for restructuring Childrens World which it bought from Boots Co and for the sale of its Blazer menswear stores to Moss Bros Plc.
Storehouse, which also owns Bhs stores, raised its interim dividend by 10 percent to 3.3 pence a share and said it planned a bigger increase in the final dividend.

"Storehouse continues to make good progress. Although the main Christmas trading period has yet to begin, the first five weeks of the second half have been encouraging," chief executive Keith Edelman said.
The results beat market forecasts and boosted Storehouse's shares, which had been weak before the results. The stock gained 13-1/2 pence to 283 before slipping back to about 275 by 1230 GMT.
"We're very pleased with the results. We think they're just a bit above the best expectations of any analyst," Edelman said.

The retailer, created by Habitat store founder Sir Terence Conran, has recovered well over the past four years from troubles brought on by overexpansion in the 1980s. But analysts have been worried lately by signs that sales have lost momentum.

Bhs and Mothercare increased sales by seven percent during the half year, assisted by new stores and overseas franchises. But a tough childrenswear market affected underlying sales at Mothercare, which fell two percent, excluding new space.
The group said it hoped to reverse the decline by the end of its current year, with Edelman saying: "We'd hope by the year end we would not be in like for like decline."
"I think we've got some work to do at Mothercare," he added, "and that's what we're focusing on now."
Management had been strengthened, splitting responsibilities for clothing and hardwear.
Corporate affairs director Richard Dixon said the chain had been recovering from the final quarter of last year when its performance had deteriorated.
Dixon said the group was introducing new ranges and he believed the stock coming in after Christmas would be stronger than last year's.

Like-for-like sales at Bhs were up about three percent, Edelman said. Overall sales at Bhs rose nine percent, of which four percent came from new stores and a further two percent from franchises overseas.

Storehouse is working to merge its Childrens World acquisition with Mothercare. It has converted four of Childrens World's 57 out-of-town sites into Mothercare World and these are generating much higher gross margins.
Storehouse bought the business from Boots for 62.5 million pounds.
Overseas, the group has opened its first Bhs franchise in Moscow and expects to have 200 international franchises for Bhs and Mothercare by the end of the year.
In Britain four new Bhs stores are planned to open before the end of March, making 140 in total. A further five or six are planned for 1997/98. ($1=.5950 Pound)
